correctness.rationale: The standard geometric blow-up gives the 56 exceptional classes in the four displayed families; for distinct curves zero numerical intersection is equivalent to disjointness. A Galois-stable disjoint seven-curve collection has a unique contraction up to isomorphism of the target, so it descends to a form of P^2; over a finite field the Brauer group is trivial. Conversely the exceptional collection of a plane contraction is stable. The least extension degree is the least Frobenius cycle length on unordered collections, not the order of Frobenius or the least degree splitting every curve. The seven reflections generate W(E7) and act faithfully because the exceptional classes span the Picard lattice. A separately written exhaustive Python/NumPy calculation rebuilt the lattice, enumerated 576 seven-cliques, closed the group and conjugacy classes under the generators, and computed cycle profiles of each representative. The 60 classes exhaust 2,903,040 elements and the exact length:count pairs were 1:694477, 2:1012627, 3:99008, 4:30240, 6:139328, 8:362880, 9:161280, 12:241920, 18:161280. The 161,280-element witness class has curve, set and quotient profiles 2^1 18^3, 18^32 and 9^32, respectively. Geiser D -> -K-D pairs distinct partners with intersection 2, so it cannot fix a disjoint collection as a set. The new calculation verifies the finite action, not the geometric classification or arithmetic realization. The latter was checked in Loughran–Trepalin Theorem 1.2 (p. 3), with no excluded fields q>=9. Replay from the workspace: python3 checks/record-2/e7_independent_check.py (NumPy); exact output alongside in e7_independent_check.log. Read the frozen census and supporting code statically, not by execution.

evidence: The old class list and stabilizer argument already give a route to max 18: W(E7) splits as Sp(6,2) times the order-two Geiser center, and the only element order above 18 in the listed classes is 30. Its sixth power has order 5, the unique order-five class, represented by a 5-cycle in the septuple S_7, so it fixes a collection.

For an order-nine element h, the characteristic polynomial on the seven-dimensional rational root space is (x-1)Phi_9(x). The cube h^3 has each primitive cube-root eigenvalue three times; an order-three element of the septuple S_7 acts as a seven-point permutation on the root space and has at most two 3-cycles, so cannot have this spectrum. The group S_7 has no order-nine element either. The order-nine action thus has every cycle of length 9, even on the quotient, since odd-order elements of the enlarged stabilizer S_7 times the Geiser center lie in S_7. Its Geiser twist g induces the same quotient action, but g^9 is Geiser and exchanges each pair, so every cycle upstairs has length 18. By the class list and Loughran–Trepalin §3 this is class 56, realized even over the smaller odd fields, beyond the frozen claim.

originality.rationale: The 56-curve lattice, the classical 288-heptad geometry, and Frobenius-class realization are prior. In fact the old group order classes plus the S_7 stabilizer give a short route to the extreme number 18 alone. The material surviving contribution is the evaluated all-class census for the actual 576-set action, with an explicitly verified descent comparison on its two-sheeted quotient. The strongest distinct same-day matches tabulate the 288-heptad action or a different, aggregated and restricted action on chambers, not the evaluated full lift.
residual_risks: An existing catalogue of the precise 576-point permutation character or the relevant marks plus power data could reduce the census to a table evaluation. The exact entry was not located in the bounded checks, and the general literature search on this record was unavailable.
Same-day quotient and chamber results are scientifically related; their order or independence cannot be inferred from the date.

The Weyl-element frequencies are not surface frequencies at a fixed field and do not decide the least field of rationality. The accepted arithmetic statement retains its stated odd-characteristic scope.

value.rationale: The census evaluates a specific arithmetic descent invariant for every Weyl type, giving the exact possible extension degrees and their distribution on the natural geometric configuration. This lets future users distinguish shortening after quotient by Geiser from actual plane descent; on the witness every degree-nine heptad still leaves the two possible contractions exchanged. The value is the complete distribution and the practical lift distinction, not recomputation of the classical number of markings or simply quoting an element of order 18.
